caption:
Oakville first home? Up to $4,000 may be claimable at closing.

Ontario's land transfer tax refund for qualifying first-time buyers is up to $4,000. It can be claimed right at registration (ask your lawyer how it is handled), or later through the Ministry of Finance within 18 months. Key conditions: you must be at least 18, a Canadian citizen or permanent resident, move in as your principal residence within nine months, and never have owned an eligible home anywhere in the world (a spouse's past ownership can also matter).

Source: Ontario.ca, "Land transfer tax refunds for first-time homebuyers" (updated Feb 10, 2026). Eligibility rules apply.

Milton, $850K home. Is 5% down enough?

Example only: $850,000 resale home, owner-occupied, minimum down payment.
1) First $500,000 x 5% = $25,000.
2) Remaining $350,000 x 10% = $35,000. Minimum down payment = $60,000.
3) Mortgage before insurance: $850,000 - $60,000 = $790,000.
4) Loan-to-value is 92.94%, so the CMHC premium rate is 4.00%: $790,000 x 4.00% = $31,600, which can be added to the mortgage ($821,600). Ontario sales tax on the premium is paid in cash at closing.
Legal fees, land transfer tax and moving costs are extra. Lenders also apply the stress test, so what you can afford may differ from what you qualify for.

Sources: Financial Consumer Agency of Canada, down payment page (modified Oct 15, 2025); CMHC premium schedule for homeowner loans.

frames.say: Milton, eight hundred fifty thousand. Minimum down payment?
Step one. The first five hundred thousand needs five percent down: twenty-five thousand dollars.
Now the twist. The rest needs ten percent: thirty-five thousand dollars. That makes sixty thousand so far.
Step three. That leaves a mortgage of seven hundred ninety thousand dollars, before mortgage insurance.
Step four. With under ten percent down, insurance may cost four percent of the loan: thirty-one thousand six hundred dollars, and it can be added to the mortgage.
So the minimum down payment on this home is sixty thousand dollars. And that is before closing costs.
Save this before you set your budget. Call nine oh five, four five two, four two nine eight.

Closing day in Halton Hills and still no keys? Here's why timing matters.

Caledon buyer: clear well water isn't always safe water.

Looking at a Caledon home with a well and septic? 1) Clear water can still carry bacteria you can't see. 2) Ask for a recent water test, and ask about making a new one an offer condition. 3) The septic system is underground; ask about an inspection and pump-out records. 4) Build both checks into your offer conditions with your realtor and lawyer.
